structured_output.summary: I changed two spots in src/execution/join_hashtable.cpp so the found-match flag is only written when it is still false. The first is the PropagatesBuildSide marking loop in ScanStructure. The second is the non-equality branch of NextRightSemiOrAntiJoin. The build succeeded (BUILD OK) and results matched in every bench run. Five bench runs of q13 against the current best gave -11.5%, +9.5%, -11.7%, +16.4% and +4.0%, which averages about +1.6% (slower). The swings are much bigger than any effect. One profile of q13.m0 showed the HASH_JOIN operator at 1.92s, against 2.15s in .dbe/profile.md. That is only one sample, and operator times are as noisy as the wall times. I see no reliable wall-time gain, so the change is unlikely to clear the 5% bar.
structured_output.generality: In principle this applies to any RIGHT or FULL OUTER hash join where build rows match many probe rows across threads. The semantics are unchanged because the only value ever written is true.
structured_output.notes: Wall time on q13 is very noisy, with ±15% swings between bench runs. That noise hides any gain from cache-coherence savings on the found flags. These stores may not be the bottleneck anyway. On q13 the bigger costs are HASH_GROUP_BY at 2.93s and the orders TABLE_SCAN with its LIKE filter at 2.75s, while HASH_JOIN is about 1.9-2.1s. If you retry this idea, combine it with something else or run many more timing repetitions. The likelier wins are the grouped aggregate on the join key (1.5M groups, count) or the NOT LIKE filter scan.
